dedupe_keys.name: myriad hes global multi hazard event sets 2004 to 2017 with the myriad hesa algorithm

description: MYRIAD-HES is a global database of historical multi-hazard event sets from 2004 to 2017 covering eleven hazards: cold waves, heatwaves, droughts, earthquakes, extreme wind, floods, landslides, tropical cyclones, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions and wildfires. Judith Claassen, Philip Ward, James Daniell, Elco Koks, Timothy Tiggeloven and Marleen de Ruiter compiled it with MYRIAD-HESA, an open algorithm that groups single-hazard footprints from varied sources, including ERA5, into events when they overlap in space within a chosen time-lag, and published both with a 2023 Scientific Reports paper that tests time-lags on North America. Coverage is global. Format and access: a CSV event table with hazard polygons in a 6.35 GB zip and a metadata PDF on Zenodo, with the algorithm released separately. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the event sets depend on the time-lag and on the resolution of each hazard source, and wildfires and ERA5-derived hazards dominate the pairs. It supports multi-hazard exposure and resilience studies where infrastructure faces hazards in close succession. Related catalogue records are the MYRIAD-EU multi-risk toolkit and the global single- and multi-hazard events dataset from EM-DAT.
